# R data types and objects

```{r type-examples}
my.number <- 3L
my.quantity <- 3.14
my.vector <- c(1,2,3)
my.string <- "Hi!"
my.factor <- factor(c("T","F"))
my.date <- Sys.Date()
my.function <- function(x){
  cat(paste("Mode of ",deparse(substitute(x))," is ",mode(x),
            "\nType of ",deparse(substitute(x))," is ",typeof(x),
            "\nClass of ",deparse(substitute(x))," is ",class(x),
            "\n",
            sep=""))
}

my.function(my.number)
my.function(my.quantity)
my.function(my.vector)
my.function(my.string)
my.function(my.factor)
my.function(my.date)
my.function(my.function)
```   
The mode and type describe what kind of information is stored in the object, while class defines methods available for the object. 

### Classes and methods

```{r class-date-difference}
class(Sys.Date() - Sys.Date())
```  

The class defines which method will be called for a function
```{r print-examples}
print(Sys.Date())
print(Sys.Date() - Sys.Date())
print(Sys.Date)
print(my.function)
print(mean)
```   

### Names and visibility

```{r namespace,error=TRUE}
mean <- c(1,2,3)
print(mean)
mean(mean)
mean <- function(){}
print(mean)
mean(mean)
mean(c(1,2,3))
base::mean(c(1,2,3))
base::mean(mean)
```   


# Amount of memory (storage)

```{r object-sizes1}
object.size(my.number)
object.size(my.quantity)
```   
```{r object-sizes2}
sapply(ls(),function(x){object.size(get(x))})
```   

```{r object-sizes3}
for(i in 1:20){
  cat(paste("The size of 1:",i," is ",object.size(1:i),"\n",sep=""))
}
```   

```{r object-sizes3.5}
object.size(1:100)
object.size(1:1000)
object.size(1:10000)
object.size(1:10000 + 1)
object.size(1:10000 + 1L)
typeof(1:10000)
typeof(1:10000 + 1)
typeof(1:10000 + 1L)
```   

# Running time

R is a very convenient programming language, but it will have performance issues unless
you use R-appropriate programming style.

### Built-in functions

```{r sum-memory-setup}
rm(list=ls())
test.length <- 1e8
data.vector <- 1:test.length
```   

A for loop for finding a sum:
```{r sum-for-loop} 
start.time <- Sys.time()
my.sum <- 0
for(i in 1:test.length){
  my.sum <- my.sum + data.vector[i]
}
my.sum
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

The built-in function for finding a sum:
```{r sum-built-in} 
start.time <- Sys.time()
sum(data.vector)
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
``` 

### Vector operations 1

```{r v1-memory-setup}
rm(list=ls())
test.length <- 1e8
pre.data.vector <- 1:test.length
``` 

A for loop for a simple operation:
```{r v1-for-loop} 
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- pre.data.vector
for(i in 1:test.length){
  post.data.vector[i] <- pre.data.vector[i] + 1L
}
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

A vectorised operation:
```{r v1-vector-op} 
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- pre.data.vector + 1L
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

### Vector operations 2

A for loop for another simple operation:
```{r v2-for-loop} 
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- pre.data.vector
for(i in 1:test.length){
  post.data.vector[i] <- pre.data.vector[i] + 1
}
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

A vectorised operation:
```{r v2-vector-op} 
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- pre.data.vector + 1
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

### Apply() family

```{r apply-memory-setup}
rm(list=ls())
test.length <- 1e7
pre.data.vector <- as.double(1:test.length)
``` 

Let's define some "complicated" processing:
```{r apply-def-function}
processing <- function(x){
  return((x^2 - 1) %% 7)
}
```   

A for loop for the complicated processing:
```{r apply-for-loop} 
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- pre.data.vector
for(i in 1:test.length){
  post.data.vector[i] <- processing(pre.data.vector[i])
}
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

`sapply()` for the complicated processing:
```{r sapply-example} 
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- sapply(pre.data.vector,processing)
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

`vapply()` for the complicated processing:
```{r vapply-example} 
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- vapply(pre.data.vector,processing,0)
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```   

A vectorised application:
```{r function-application}
rm(post.data.vector)
start.time <- Sys.time()
post.data.vector <- processing(pre.data.vector)
end.time <- Sys.time()
print(end.time - start.time)
```

https://app.datacamp.com/learn/courses/writing-efficient-r-code.
